Assuming that the factors applied to extrapolate the signal and reference-channel branching fractions from the phase space defined in Table 1 to the full phase space approximately cancel in the ratio, we use the measured value of \(\mathcal{B}(Z\to\mu^{+}\mu^{-}\mu^{-})=(1.20\pm 0.08)\times 10^{-6}\)[4] for \(m(\mu^{+}\mu^{-})>4\) GeV to obtain an estimate for \(\mathcal{B}(Z\to J/\psi\ell^{+}\ell^{-})\) of \(8\times 10^{-7}\)

name: Figure 3
mentions: Figure 3 displays the ratios of the measured \(\Delta\varphi_{\rm{dijet}}\) distributions to the next-to-leading-order (NLO) predictions of pQCD calculations from the parton-level generator NLOjet++[21] within the fast NLO framework [22]

Figure 1: Feynman diagrams of the \(t\)-channel single top quark production at LO corresponding to four- (left) and five-flavor (right) schemes

The second b jet, arising in the production process via gluon splitting, as shown in figure 1 (left), has a softer \(p_{\mathrm{T}}\) spectrum and a broader pseudorapidity \(\eta\) distribution compared to the b jet originating from the top quark, and thus frequently escapes detection
The signal process [32] is simulated with powheg 2.0 in the four-flavor scheme (4FS), where b quarks are produced via gluon splitting as shown in figure 1 (left)
This scheme is expected to yield a more accurate description of the kinematic distributions of \(t\)-channel events than the five-flavor scheme (5FS) [33, 34, 35] indicated in figure 1 (right)

name: Figure 1
mentions: Examples of leading order (LO) diagrams describing the \(\mathrm{H}^{\pm}\) production in 2HDM in different mass regions are shown in figure 1

Light \(\mathrm{H}^{\pm}\), with a mass smaller than the mass difference between the top and the bottom quarks (\(m_{\mathrm{H}^{\pm}}<m_{\mathrm{t}}-m_{\mathrm{b}}\)), are predominantly produced in decays of top quarks (double-resonant top quark production, figure 1 left), whereas heavy \(\mathrm{H}^{\pm}\) (\(m_{\mathrm{H}^{\pm}}>m_{\mathrm{t}}-m_{\mathrm{b}}\)) are produced in association with a top quark as \(\mathrm{p}\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{t}\mathrm{b}\mathrm{H}^{\pm}\) (single-resonant top quark production, figure 1 middle)

Light \(\mathrm{H}^{\pm}\), with a mass smaller than the mass difference between the top and the bottom quarks (\(m_{\mathrm{H}^{\pm}}<m_{\mathrm{t}}-m_{\mathrm{b}}\)), are predominantly produced in decays of top quarks (double-resonant top quark production, figure 1 left), whereas heavy \(\mathrm{H}^{\pm}\) (\(m_{\mathrm{H}^{\pm}}>m_{\mathrm{t}}-m_{\mathrm{b}}\)) are produced in association with a top quark as \(\mathrm{p}\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{t}\mathrm{b}\mathrm{H}^{\pm}\) (single-resonant top quark production, figure 1 middle)

In the intermediate region near the mass of the top quark (\(m_{\mathrm{H}^{\pm}}\sim m_{\mathrm{t}}\)), the nonresonant top quark production mode (figure 1 right) also contributes and the full \(\mathrm{p}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{H}^{\pm}\mathrm{W}^{\mp}\mathrm{b} \overline{\mathrm{b}}\) process must be calculated in order to correctly account for all three production mechanisms and their interference [20].

mentions: The pair production of any of the combinations \(\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\), \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\), \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\), or \(\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\) is allowed [28], enhancing the effective cross section for the \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\) di-higgsino state and thus for \(hh\) and \(hZ\) production [Fig. 1 (left) and (center)]

As a second specific example of a SUSY scenario with Higgs bosons, we consider the R-parity-conserving chargino-neutralino \(\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\) electroweak pair production process shown in Fig. 1 (right), in which the \(\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\) chargino is winolike and the \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\) neutralino is a massive, stable, weakly interacting binolike LSP, where a bino is the SUSY partner of the \(B\) gauge boson

For the GMSB scenarios [Fig. 1 (left) and (center)], the \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\), \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\), and \(\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\) particles are taken to be mass-degenerate pure higgsing states, such that any SM particles arising from the decays of the \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\) and \(\tilde{\chi}^{+}_{1}\) states to the \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\) state are too soft to be detected

For the electroweak \(hW\) scenario [Fig. 1 (right)], we make the simplifying assumption \(m_{\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}}=m_{\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}}\)[36] and generate event samples for a range of \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\) and LSP (\(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\)) mass values, with the decays of the \(\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\) chargino and \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\) neutralino described using the bridge v2.24 program [70]
The signal events correspond to the higgsino pair production scenario of Fig. 1 (left) with a higgsino (\(\tilde{\chi}_{1}^{0}\)) mass of 250 GeV and an LSP (gravitino) mass of 1 GeV.
The SUSY scenarios of interest to this study (Fig. 1) can yield events with three or more leptons if the \(h\), \(Z\), or \(W\) bosons decay to final states with leptons
The three-or-more-lepton results provide sensitivity to the SUSY \(ZZ\) channel, i.e., to events in which the two Higgs bosons in Fig. 1 (left) are each replaced by a \(Z\) boson
Reference [36] also contains results on the \(hW\) signal scenario of Fig. 1 (right) in decay channels that are complementary to those considered here

Following our discussion of the GMSB model, we present limits for the electroweak chargino-neutralino pair production process of Fig. 1 (right) as a function of the LSP (\(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\)) and common \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2},\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\) masses, taking the \(\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\to h\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\) and \(\tilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\to W^{\pm}\tilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\) branching fractions each to be unity.

We find empirically, through studies with simulation, that the shape of the \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) distribution is similar for all top-quark and \(W+\mathbf{j}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{s}\) background categories that enter the signal (Table 1) or sideband (\(150<E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}<250\) GeV) regions, regardless of whether the \(W\) boson decays to \(e\), \(\mu\), or \(\tau\), or whether a \(\tau\) lepton decays hadronically or leptonically: The decay of the \(W\) boson in \(W+\mathbf{j}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{s}\) events generates an \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) spectrum (from the neutrino) that is similar to the \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) spectrum generated by the \(W\) boson produced directly in the decay of a top quark in top-quark events

Based on these observations, we implement a template method in which the shape of the \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) distribution in an SL sample is used to describe the shape of the \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) distribution in the corresponding signal sample of Table 1, for all top-quark and \(W+\mathbf{j}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{s}\) categories

We split each SL sample into a sideband \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) region SB-SL defined by \(150<E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}<250\) GeV, and a signal \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) region SIG-SL given by the corresponding \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) requirement in Table 1

The templates are normalized based on the number of top-quark plus \(W+\mathbf{j}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{s}\) events observed in the SB regions (\(150<E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}<250\) GeV) of samples selected with the requirements of Table 1 except for that on \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\)

The \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) SB region corresponds to \(150<E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}<250\) GeV while the SIG regions correspond to the \(E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}\) regions listed in Table 1

In fact, as shown in figure 1, this production mode leads to final states with one top quark and an additional jet, which tends to be in the forward region of the detector, while the additionally produced b quark is typically low in \(p_{\mathrm{T}}\) and therefore is not reconstructed

Furthermore, in the wino-like case, the expected event yields for the single-photon and diphoton analyses are reduced since the chargino (neutralino) may decay to a W (Z) and the gravitino (see figure 1).

mentions: Examples of invariant mass distributions of reconstructed \(\mathrm{K_{S}^{0}}\) and \(\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda}\) candidates are shown in Fig. 1 for pPb data, with \(V^{0}\)\(p_{\mathrm{T}}\) in the range of 1-3 GeV and event multiplicity in the range \(220\leq N_{\mathrm{trk}}^{\mathrm{ offline}}<260\)

The true \(V^{0}\) signal peak is well described by a double Gaussian function (with a common mean), while the background is modeled by a 4th-order polynomial function fit over the entire mass range shown in Fig. 1

The mass window of \(\pm 2\sigma\) wide around the center of the peak is defined as the "peak region", where \(\sigma\) represents the root mean square of the two standard deviations of the double Gaussian functions weighted by the yields (with typical value of \(\sigma\) indicated in Fig. 1)

To estimate the contribution of background candidates in the peak region to the correlation measurement, a "sideband region" is chosen that includes \(V^{0}\) candidates from outside the \(\pm 3\sigma\) mass range around the \(V^{0}\) mass to the limit of the mass distributions shown in Fig. 1.
Here, \(f^{\rm sig}\) represents the signal yield fraction in the peak region determined by the fits to the mass distribution shown in Fig. 1

name: Figure 1
mentions: At the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), exclusive \(\gamma\gamma\) (hereafter referred to as "diphoton") events can be produced by means of \(\mathrm{IPIP}\) exchange, interpreted in partonic terms as \(\mathrm{gg}\to\gamma\gamma\)via a quark loop, with an additional "screening" gluon exchanged to cancel the color of the interacting gluons, as shown in figure 1(a)

name: Figure 1
mentions: Two \(\tau\) leptons can be generated in the decay chain of \(\widetilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\) and \(\widetilde{\tau}\), as shown in figure 1
Figure 1: Schematic production of \(\tau\) lepton pairs from chargino (left) or \(\tau\) slepton (right) pair production.

In one of the signal samples, pairs of charginos are produced with pythia 6.426 and decayed exclusively to the final states that contain two \(\tau\) leptons, two \(\tau\) neutrinos, and two neutralinos, as shown in figure 1 (left)

In this scenario, no decay modes are considered other than those shown in figure 1 (left), so for \(\mathrm{m}(\widetilde{\tau})=\mathrm{m}(\widetilde{\nu}_{\tau})\), the two decay chains (via the \(\widetilde{\tau}\) or \(\widetilde{\nu}_{\tau}\)) have 50% branching fraction
In the other signal sample, pairs of staus are also produced with pythia 6.426, that decay always to two \(\tau\) leptons and two neutralinos, figure 1 (right)
These results are interpreted in the context of a simplified model of chargino pair production and decay, which is described in section 3 and corresponds to the left diagram in figure 1.
The results are also interpreted to set limits on \(\widetilde{\tau}\widetilde{\tau}\) production, which corresponds to the right diagram in figure 1

name: Figure 1
mentions: Elastic light-by-light (LbL) scattering, \(\gamma\gamma\to\gamma\gamma\), is a pure quantum mechanical process that proceeds, at leading order in the quantum electrodynamics (QED) coupling \(\alpha\), via virtual box diagrams containing charged particles (Fig. 1, left)

The final-state signature of interest in this analysis is the exclusive production of two photons, \(\mathrm{PbPb}\to\gamma\gamma\to\mathrm{Pb}^{(*)}\gamma\gamma\mathrm{Pb}^{(*)}\), where the diphoton final state is measured in the otherwise empty central part of the detector, and the outgoing Pb ions (with a potential electromagnetic excitation denoted by the (\({}^{*}\)) superscript) survive the interaction and escape undetected at very low \(\theta\) angles with respect to the beam direction (Fig. 1, left)

The dominant backgrounds are the QED production of an exclusive electron-positron pair (\(\gamma\gamma\to\mathrm{e}^{+}\mathrm{e}^{-}\)) where the \(\mathrm{e}^{\pm}\) are misidentified as photons (Fig. 1, centre), and gluon-induced central exclusive production (CEP) [25] of a pair of photons (Fig
1, centre), and gluon-induced central exclusive production (CEP) [25] of a pair of photons (Fig. 1, right).
new heavy particles, such as magnetic monopoles [27], vector-like fermions [28], or dark sector particles [29], contribute to the virtual corrections of the box depicted in Fig. 1

Another model, referred to as T5qqqqWZ, involves gluino pair production, where each gluino decays to a pair of light quarks (u, d, s, and c) and a neutralino (\(\widetilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\)) or chargino (\(\widetilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\)), followed by decay of the neutralino or the chargino to a W or Z boson, respectively, and the LSP (Fig. 1--middle)
A model called T6ttWW, features bottom squark pair production with their subsequent cascade decays via top quarks and W bosons(Fig. 1--bottom)

mentions: Examples for SUSY processes that can give rise to multilepton final states are shown in figure 1

A typical process predicted by SUSY models consists of gluino pair production with each gluino decaying to a top quark pair, \(\rm t\overline{t}\), and an LSP, \(\widetilde{\chi}^{0}_{1}\) (figure 1, upper left), or to a pair of quarks and a neutralino, \(\widetilde{\chi}^{0}_{2}\), or chargino, \(\widetilde{\chi}^{\pm}_{1}\)
The latter would then decay into a Z or W boson, and an LSP (figure 1, upper right)

Other models feature bottom squark, \(\widetilde{\rm b}_{1}\), pair production, with subsequent cascade decays resulting in top quarks, W bosons and LSPs (figure 1, lower left) or pair production of the heaviest of the two top squark states, \(\widetilde{\rm t}_{2}\), with subsequent decays to top quarks, Higgs or Z bosons, and LSPs (figure 1, lower right)

Other models feature bottom squark, \(\widetilde{\rm b}_{1}\), pair production, with subsequent cascade decays resulting in top quarks, W bosons and LSPs (figure 1, lower left) or pair production of the heaviest of the two top squark states, \(\widetilde{\rm t}_{2}\), with subsequent decays to top quarks, Higgs or Z bosons, and LSPs (figure 1, lower right)
